text:
eli: Heads-up — after landing the kernel prefetch change last night we see an ~18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on canary, and p95 latency increased by ~22ms for short-context workloads. Repro steps and short profiler dump below.

maria: ack — can you paste the numbers and which model/slot?

eli: Canary: model rdx-13b-q4f, slot gpu-a1. Hit-rate: baseline 72% -> canary 59%. p50 token-latency: 6.8ms -> 9.1ms, p95: 32ms -> 54ms. Resource utilization didn't spike.

sam: interesting. so CPU or kernel change affected cache keying? any change to key hashing or batching order? :thinking_face:

eli: The kernel prefetch introduces a small reordering to favor kernel-ready batches (microbatch re-shuffle). That means continuous-batcher sometimes groups requests with slightly different prefix keys into the same microbatch and we observed cache-miss amplification.

kai: do we have flamegraphs or perf stats that show cache miss vs reorder events?

eli: Quick profiler snippet from tracing session (reduced):

```
trace: request_id=abcd1234
batch_compose: microbatch_id=472 reorder=true
kv_lookup: keys=8 hits=3 misses=5
runtime_exec: kernel_prefetch=true, kernel_choice=triton_v2
latency_tokens_ms: [1.2,0.9,...] total=48.7
```

eli: Also ran a targeted A/B: disabling prefetch (but keeping kernel selection) restores hit-rate to ~71% so the prefetch reordering looks causal.

frank: wow. that matches an hypoth we had about ordering + prefix-key collisions. Are we keying on full prefix hash or something with non-deterministic components?

eli: We key on (model, version, prefix_hash, slice_group). The prefetch flow was adding ephemeral affinity tags to batches that altered slice_group assignment for a minority of requests. Those tags were not part of the hash, but the slice_group ended up being different so warm KV entries landed in different cache partitions.

maria: can you paste the batching config changes from the PR?

eli: From the PR:
```
# old
continuous_batch_window_ms: 8
microbatch_reorder_enabled: false
# new
continuous_batch_window_ms: 6
microbatch_reorder_enabled: true
kernel_prefetch: true
```

anya: so smaller window + reordering = more mixing across cohorts — warmups less effective. makes sense.

sam: what about making keying include the deterministic cohort ID so reordering doesn't move warm entries? or sticky affinity so a request keeps its cohort while in the queue?

eli: options we discussed:
- roll back microbatch reordering (fast mitigation)
- include affinity_bucket in cache key (longer term but potentially increases fragmentation)
- implement soft stickiness (bind request to cohort for up to X ms while warmup active)
- gate kernel prefetch so it doesn't reorder for prefixes below a hit-rate threshold

kai: would including affinity_bucket in key cause cache fragmentation enough to hurt overall hit-rate? We should simulate.

frank: I can run a quick sim using production trace sampler — compare effective hit-rate if key space expands by +10% vs +40%. Give me a couple hours.

eli: thanks. I'm leaning to gating prefetch for now and adding stickiness in the short term. We should also add metrics: microbatch_reorder=true hit-rate, and a histogram of slice_group churn per request.

maria: deploy-bot: any canary alerts?

deploy-bot: alert: canary rdx-13b-q4f experienced prefix-cache-hit-rate drop of 18% at 2026-03-17T03:12:14Z. Automatic rollback not triggered.

sam: can we quickly test a config patch that disables reorder but leaves kernel_prefetch on (i.e., prefetch without reordering)? that would indicate whether prefetch itself or reorder is root cause.

eli: good idea. I'm spinning a canary with microbatch_reorder_enabled=false, kernel_prefetch=true. I'll post the ts when up.

(20m later)

eli: canary up: thread_ts=2210001170. Initial numbers: hit-rate back to 70%, p95 down to 35ms. So reordering is the main culprit.

sam: nice. so next steps: roll back reorder flag in the release, add a follow-up to implement gating + soft-stickiness, and run frank's fragmentation sim. Also add a short-term metric for "cohort_stability".

frank: sim started on trace-sample-20260316, will share results within 3h.

anya: owner for rollback? eli or infra?

eli: I'll submit hotfix PR to flip microbatch_reorder_enabled=false and include a comment to avoid full revert of kernel_prefetch.

maria: add an eval run for user-workload mix (short prompts heavy) — make sure we don't regress latency improvements for long-context cases when we disable reorder.

eli: noted. I suspect long-context p50 won't change much; reorder helped some kernel utilization cases. We'll try a targeted canary to balance.

sam: put remediation checklist in the PR: metric assertions, canary thresholds (hit-rate delta <3%), and rollback criteria.

eli: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:

frank: preliminary sim note: adding affinity_bucket to keyspace reduces cross-cohort misses but increases cold-start misses by 6% in sim. Full results tbd.

maria: thanks — keep us posted. we'll pause other kernel prefetch changes until this is sorted.

eli: summary action items:
- eli: open hotfix PR to disable microbatch_reorder (in progress)
- frank: simulate fragmentation impact of adding affinity_bucket to cache key (3h)
- sam: add metric "cohort_stability" and microbatch_reorder boolean to per-route dashboards
- maria: run eval suite for short-prompt dominated workloads after hotfix

eli: linking PR in thread when ready.

(ended)
